answer: In a juniper timber market, a registry issues one signed receipt per independently inspected shipment. The payment kernel verifies the signature and marks the canonical shipment ID spent after paying one fixed bounty. A thousand agent aliases cannot redeem that shipment again. Extra rewards require distinct inspected deliveries, with real timber and audit costs. Auditors must prevent duplicate IDs for the same cargo; otherwise the attacker clones receipts instead of identities.
